subfamily: julep: the Codex's Mint Julep (pp. 30-31, an Old-Fashioned with mint for the bitters), made in the ode's order with the ode's rich syrup, on ice pounded in a canvas bag (McMillian, Oxford pdf 1273 / ICE MALLET pdf 1066)
glass: julep cup (pewter or stainless steel; any metal tumbler of about 300 ml at home), heaped with ice pounded in a canvas bag
version: v1.1 (Tomás, round 4: glass wording per Hester T1; no number moves). v1 (Tomás, round 2, 2026-10-04). Codex p. 31: 60 bourbon, 7.5 simple, rub the tin with mint, crushed ice, churn to frost. Mine: 7.5 ml RICH syrup (2:1; the ode's sugar mixed into cold water 'till it seems like oil') for the simple, +2.1 g sugar; the ode's order (bourbon over the ice first, the syrup poured over it), then the Codex's churn to frost (the ode says no stirring: departure owned, and an unstirred sweet layer is No Accident's ground). Freeform: a julep keeps melting; served case modelled with 30 ml melt (water line), swept 15-45 ml and judged by hand against Arnold's built band. Bourbon a style, 45% modelled; swept 40-50%. No added spark ingredient: Matrix consulted and set aside (Checks).
